job_title: Postdoctoral Research Fellowship: Wildlife Science, Wildlife Management and Conservation Biology (1-
about_role:
The Department of Animal Science at the University of the Free State (UFS), South Africa, invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Fellowship in Wildlife Science, Wildlife Management and Conservation Biology.
Candidates interested in pursuing an academic or professional career in Wildlife Science, Wildlife Management, Conservation Biology, Rangeland Ecology, Wildlife Monitoring and Sustainable Natural Resource Management are encouraged to apply.
The successful candidate will join an active multidisciplinary research programme focused on understanding the ecological, biological, nutritional and conservation factors regulating African wildlife populations, with particular emphasis on large herbivores, habitat utilisation, wildlife monitoring, sustainable rangeland management and evidence-based conservation planning.
The fellowship provides an opportunity for a talented doctoral graduate to gain advanced research, teaching and postgraduate supervision experience under the mentorship of established researchers while contributing to internationally recognised research programmes.
The fellowship will be awarded on a competitive basis, considering applicants' academic achievements, publication record, teaching experience, supervisory experience and research potential. The fellowship is available for a period of one year and is renewable annually for up to three years, subject to satisfactory performance and the submission of annual progress reports.
Duties and responsibilities:
•    Conduct innovative research in wildlife science, wildlife management and conservation biology.
•    Contribute to research on wildlife monitoring, habitat assessment, sustainable rangeland management, conservation planning and large herbivore ecology.
•    Utilise modern technologies including GPS telemetry, GIS, remote sensing, drones and artificial intelligence within wildlife research programmes.
•    Publish a minimum of two peer-reviewed scientific papers per year.
•    Present research findings at national and international scientific conferences.
•    Assist with undergraduate teaching and practical training in Wildlife Science and Wildlife Management.
•    Assist with the supervision and mentoring of Honours, MSc and PhD students.
•    Contribute to curriculum enhancement and module development.
•    Assist with grant applications and research project development.
•    Register and reside as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of the Free State and participate in relevant activities of the Directorate of Research and Postgraduate Studies.
Job Requirements:
Eligibility criteria
•    Open to all South African and foreign nationals for full-time research at the University of the Free State.
•    Hold a PhD degree in Wildlife Science, Wildlife Management, Conservation Biology, Ecology, Zoology, Rangeland Science, Animal Science or a closely related discipline.
•    Have obtained their doctoral degree within the last five years.
•    Demonstrate a publication record in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
•    Have experience in wildlife research and field-based ecological studies
•    Demonstrate experience in undergraduate teaching and practical training.
•    Demonstrate the ability to contribute to curriculum development and postgraduate supervision.
•    Possess excellent scientific writing and communication skills.
•    Hold a valid driver's licence (attach a copy).
•    Successful applicants may not hold full-time salaried employment during the fellowship period.
•    Successful applicants must be willing to relocate to Bloemfontein and participate fully in departmental research, teaching and postgraduate activities.
Application:
To apply, please email the following documentation by 21 August 2026 to Prof Francois Deacon at deaconf@ufs.ac.za. Late applications will not be considered.
•    Motivation letter detailing research experience, teaching experience, publication record and suitability for the fellowship.
•    Full Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications, conference presentations and other scholarly outputs.
•    Full academic transcripts and copy of doctoral degree certificate.
•    Copy of ID document or passport.
•    Contact details of three academic referees.
Value of the fellowship:
•    R 270,000 annual fellowship.
•    R 30,000 additional research expenses fund.
Closing date:
21 August 2026
Commencement of fellowship:
01 January 2027

about_role:
The University of the Free State invites applications from visionary, innovative and strategic leaders for the position of Senior Director: Directorate for Institutional Research, Strategic Analytics and Institutional Effectiveness and Planning (DIRSIP). Reporting to the Deputy Vice-Chancellor: Strategic Initiatives, International and Institutional Affairs, the Senior Director provides strategic leadership for institutional planning, strategy implementation, institutional research, business intelligence, statutory reporting, project portfolio management and enrolment planning.
The incumbent will play a pivotal role in supporting evidence-based decision-making, organisational effectiveness and the successful implementation of the University's Vision 130 and strategic priorities.  As a member of the University's senior leadership community, the successful candidate will lead the University's institutional planning and performance management functions while ensuring that strategic information supports sound governance and executive decision-making.
Duties and responsibilities​​​​
Strategic Plan Tracking
•    Coordinate the implementation of Vision 130, the Strategic Plan, and the Annual Performance Plan.
•    Steer strategy, institutional research and operational projects.
•    Monitor the Key Performance Indicators across all portfolios, faculties and divisions.
Executive Decision Support
•    Produce the University of the Free State’s annual report to Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET), mid-term review report, and student enrolment plan, which are aligned with the academic risk register.
•    Steer the UFS to a forward-looking strategic institution by leading business intelligence information needs, translating complex institutional data into high-level briefings, providing predictive analytics, trend mapping, and data modelling
•    Facilitate HEMIS data submissions.
Global Benchmarking
•    Utilise institutional data for global positioning, supporting the university’s internationalisation mandate and rankings.
•    Manage data to be submitted to global rankings bodies.
Institutional Effectiveness and Optimisation
•    Lead institutional initiatives that identify operational bottlenecks and resource allocation efficiencies to drive overall institutional effectiveness.
•    Lead the Institutional Project Management Office.
•    Develop and maintain institutional project governance frameworks.
•    Coordinate, monitor and evaluate strategic institutional projects funded through the University's strategic initiatives.
•    Monitor institutional project performance, risks and benefits realisation.
•    Provide executive reports on strategic project implementation.
Institutional Strategy and Planning
•    Lead the development, implementation and monitoring of the University's Strategic Plan, Annual Performance Plan and institutional performance framework.
•    Coordinate institutional planning processes and monitor progress against strategic objectives.
•    Provide strategic advice to Executive Management on institutional performance, organisational effectiveness and strategic initiatives.
•    Lead institutional change management initiatives supporting strategic transformation.
Institutional Research and Business Intelligence
•    Direct institutional research and policy analysis to support executive decision-making.
•    Develop and maintain an integrated institutional management information and business intelligence environment.
•    Produce executive dashboards, strategic reports and institutional analyses that inform planning, policy development and performance improvement.
•    Promote evidence-based decision-making throughout the University.
Institutional Data Governance and Statutory Reporting
•    Provide strategic leadership for institutional data governance and data quality management.
•    Oversee HEMIS submissions and all statutory reporting to the Department of Higher Education and Training and other regulatory authorities.
•    Ensure compliance with legislative, audit and quality assurance requirements.
•    Develop institutional data policies, standards and governance frameworks.
Enrolment Planning and Performance Monitoring
•    Lead institutional enrolment planning and student performance analysis.
•    Develop forecasting models and strategic enrolment scenarios.
•    Monitor institutional performance indicators and benchmarking against national and international best practice.
•    Produce the University's Annual Report, Mid-term Review Report and other strategic institutional reports.
Stakeholder Engagement
•    Develop strategic partnerships with government departments, regulatory authorities, professional bodies, universities and national higher education structures.
•    Represent the University on institutional and national committees relating to planning, institutional research and higher education policy.
•    Manage data to be submitted to global rankings bodies
Leadership and Directorate Management
•    Provide strategic leadership to the Directorate.
•    Translate institutional strategy into operational plans and measurable performance outcomes.
•    Lead organisational development, succession planning, talent management and staff development.
•    Manage the Directorate's human, financial and physical resources in accordance with University policies.
Inherent Job Requirements
•    A relevant Doctoral qualification on NQF Level 10 in Higher Education Management, Strategy, Public Administration, Business Administration, Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems or a related field.
•    A minimum of seven (7) years' experience within the higher education sector.
•    At least five (5) years in a senior strategic leadership role.
•    Experience in institutional strategy development and implementation.
•    Experience in institutional research and higher education policy analysis.
•    Experience in business intelligence and management information systems.
•    Experience in data governance, HEMIS and statutory reporting.
•    Experience in institutional project portfolio management.
•    Executive stakeholder engagement and organisational leadership experience.
Recommendations
•    A postgraduate qualification in Higher Education Management, Strategy, Public Administration, Business Administration, Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems or a related field.
•    Knowledge of South African higher education policy, funding and quality assurance frameworks.
•    Experience in digital transformation, data analytics and institutional performance management.
•    Experience leading complex organisational change initiatives.
•    Advanced knowledge of business intelligence platforms and data visualisation.

Term of Appointment
The Senior Director will be appointed on a five-year fixed-term performance-based contract in accordance with the University's policies and procedures and may be eligible for reappointment subject to institutional requirements and performance.

job_title: Senior Infrastructure Demand Management Server Coordinator
about_role:
ROLE PURPOSE
The Senior Infrastructure Demand Management – Server Lead is accountable for end‑to‑end ownership and governance of server infrastructure demand across physical, virtual, and cloud environments. The role provides senior technical and service leadership to ensure that infrastructure demand is optimally planned, prioritised, governed, and delivered in alignment with business strategy, client commitments, security standards, and service management frameworks.
The incumbent acts as the primary authority on server demand intake, demand shaping, and delivery readiness, translating complex business and project requirements into executable infrastructure demand plans. The role operates with a high degree of autonomy, influencing delivery outcomes across multiple technical teams, and ensuring infrastructure demand is delivered predictably, compliantly, and at scale.
ROLE REQUIREMENT
• Strategic Infrastructure Demand Ownership
• Own and govern the server infrastructure demand pipeline across physical, virtual, and cloud platforms.
• Shape demand through early engagement with business, programme, and project stakeholders to ensure feasibility, cost awareness, and technical alignment.
• Act as the senior escalation point for complex or high‑risk infrastructure demand initiatives.
• Influence prioritisation decisions to balance capacity, risk, cost, and delivery commitments.
• Senior Build Governance & Delivery Enablement
• Translate approved demand into standardised, scalable build architectures and demand artefacts for execution by infrastructure engineering teams.
• Provide senior oversight of server build readiness, ensuring all technical, security, and operational prerequisites are met before execution.
• Govern complex builds, migrations, and environment expansions, including hybrid and cloud‑integrated solutions.
• Ensure infrastructure delivery adheres to agreed architectural, operational, and service standards.
• Service Management Leadership & SLA Assurance
• Provide senior operational leadership across the full lifecycle of infrastructure requests, from demand intake to production handover.
• Monitor delivery performance against SLAs, KPIs, and contractual commitments, proactively addressing systemic issues.
• Drive alignment with ITIL practices across Incident, Change, Problem, and Release processes.
• Champion service stability, predictability, and continuous service improvement.
• CMDB, Data Integrity & Asset Governance
• Own the accuracy, integrity, and auditability of server configuration items within the CMDB.
• Define and enforce standards for CI lifecycle management, data quality, and reconciliation.
• Lead investigations into CMDB discrepancies and implement corrective and preventative actions.
• Ensure infrastructure assets are fully traceable, compliant, and governance‑ready at all times.
• Security, Compliance & Risk Management
• Ensure all server infrastructure demand complies with organisational security, risk, and regulatory requirements prior to production release.
• Coordinate senior‑level sign‑offs with Information Security, Risk, and Compliance stakeholders.
• Identify infrastructure‑related risks early and drive mitigation strategies across delivery teams.
• Support internal and external audits by providing authoritative infrastructure evidence and documentation.
• Reporting, Optimization & Continuous Improvement
• Produce executive‑level reporting on infrastructure demand trends, delivery performance, capacity constraints, and risk exposure.
• Analyze demand data to inform forecasting, capacity planning, and investment decisions.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on automation, standardization, and process efficiency.
• Act as a thought leader within infrastructure demand management, contributing to best practice and maturity uplift.
PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES
• Deep understanding of Windows and Linux server environments (physical, virtual, and cloud)
• Advanced knowledge of virtualisation platforms (e.g. VMware)
• Strong exposure to cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or equivalent)
• Expert use of ITSM tools (e.g. BMC Remedy, ServiceNow, Jira)
• Strong command of ITIL‑aligned service management practices
• Advanced understanding of CMDB architecture and configuration management
• Ability to translate technical complexity into business‑relevant insights
QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
• Grade 12
• Diploma or Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related discipline
• 10–15 years’ experience in enterprise ICT infrastructure, with demonstrated senior accountability
• 5+ years’ experience operating in complex, multi‑stakeholder delivery or project environments
• ITIL Foundation certification (required); ITIL Intermediate or equivalent advantageous
• Proven experience across server hardware, operating systems, storage, and networking
• Enterprise‑scale exposure to hybrid and cloud infrastructure environments Experience in server infrastructure (hardware, OS, storage, networking)
• Working knowledge of BMC Remedy or similar ITSM tool
• Exposure to cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Azure) advantageous

Your job: get on the phone, explain the process, handle the objections, and move them down the line toward getting licensed.
These are government-regulated licences — a legal requirement to work in their trade. The customer needs this. We just make it faster and simpler than doing it alone. That makes the sale close to a no-brainer, and your job is to push it over the line.

• You understand the importance of speed to lead.

Icon Healthcare is seeking an experienced and hands-on Health, Safety & Environmental Manager to coordinate and support Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) activities across our national healthcare operations. Reporting to the Group Chief Operating Officer, this role will partner with operational management to ensure legislative compliance, promote a proactive safety culture and drive continuous improvement across the Group's oncology, renal, pharmacy and technical services businesses.
This is an ideal opportunity for an experienced HSE professional who enjoys working operationally across multiple sites. The successful candidate will initially have no direct reports and will work collaboratively with operational management, clinical teams, contractors and external regulatory authorities to influence best practice and ensure consistent implementation of Health, Safety and Environmental standards across the Group.
Key Responsibilities:
• Develop, implement and maintain a comprehensive occupational health and safety framework across all IHH operations
• Ensure compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act, Radiation Control Regulations, Pharmacy Council standards, environmental regulations and healthcare accreditation requirements
• Conduct enterprise-wide health and safety risk assessments, identify hazards, implement corrective actions and lead investigations into incidents, injuries, near misses and environmental events
• Support management and employees with COIDA-related processes, including injury-on-duty reporting, Compensation Fund submissions, incident investigations, return-to-work programmes and compliance with applicable legislative requirements
• Monitor and coordinate safety compliance within radiation oncology facilities, chemotherapy pharmacies, renal treatment centres and technical engineering environments in partnership with operational leaders and external specialists
• Develop and facilitate safety training, toolbox talks, emergency preparedness drills and awareness programmes for employees, contractors and service providers nationally
• Lead internal and external HSE audits, maintain safety statistics and dashboards, compile executive reports and drive continuous improvement initiatives
• Act as the primary liaison between the Group and relevant regulatory authorities
• Manage contractor compliance, construction safety, facilities inspections and project-related safety requirements across all national sites
• Regular national travel to Group facilities will be required

The Marketing Assistant will provide comprehensive marketing and administrative support to the Marketing Department to ensure the successful planning, coordination, implementation, and reporting of all marketing initiatives. The role is responsible for enhancing the shopping centre's brand, driving foot traffic, increasing customer engagement, and supporting tenant marketing activities through both traditional and digital marketing channels.
The successful candidate will have a strong marketing background with proven experience in developing and executing marketing campaigns. They must be highly proficient in social media management, digital marketing, content creation, and project coordination, while demonstrating exceptional organisational and administrative skills to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced retail environment.
KEY RESPONSBILITIES
Marketing Campaign Planning & Execution
• Assist in the planning, implementation, coordination, and evaluation of marketing campaigns, promotions, and events.
• Coordinate marketing initiatives with tenants, agencies, suppliers, media partners, and other stakeholders.
• Ensure campaigns are executed on time, within budget, and in line with the shopping centre's marketing strategy and brand guidelines.
• Support the delivery of shopping centre events, activations, exhibitions, competitions, and community initiatives.
• Monitor campaign performance and compile post-campaign evaluations with recommendations for future improvements.
Social Media & Digital Marketing
• Manage the shopping centre's social media platforms by planning, creating, scheduling, publishing, and monitoring engaging content.
• Develop creative digital content, including copywriting, photography, short-form videos, and promotional material that strengthens brand awareness and customer engagement.

• Assist with digital advertising campaigns, website updates, email marketing, and other online communication channels.
• Monitor digital marketing performance and prepare regular analytics and performance reports.
Content Development
• Create compelling marketing content for social media, websites, email campaigns, in-centre digital screens, promotional materials, and advertising campaigns.
• Liaise with graphic designers, photographers, videographers, printers, and other service providers to ensure high-quality marketing collateral is delivered.
• Ensure all marketing content is accurate, on-brand, and aligned with campaign objectives.
Project Coordination
• Coordinate multiple marketing projects simultaneously while maintaining strict adherence to deadlines and budgets.
• Maintain project schedules, campaign calendars, and implementation timelines.
• Follow up with internal departments, tenants, suppliers, and external service providers to ensure projects are completed successfully.
• Assist with campaign planning, logistics, reporting, and project close-out activities.
Administration & Reporting
• Provide comprehensive administrative support to the Marketing Department.
• Maintain organised marketing calendars, filing systems, databases, and marketing asset libraries.
• Coordinate supplier quotations, purchase orders, invoices, and payment processes.
• Assist with budget administration, expenditure tracking, and reconciliation.
• Prepare meeting agendas, minutes, presentations, reports, and marketing documentation.
• Compile monthly marketing reports, social media analytics, campaign summaries, and performance dashboards.
• Maintain accurate records of all marketing campaigns, promotions, events, and supplier information.
Stakeholder & Tenant Relations
• Build and maintain positive relationships with tenants, suppliers, media partners, agencies, and service providers.
• Assist tenants with marketing opportunities and promotional activities where required.
• Coordinate communication between internal departments and external stakeholders to ensure the smooth execution of marketing initiatives.
General Responsibilities
• Stay informed of current marketing trends, consumer behaviour, digital platforms, and industry best practices.
• Identify opportunities to improve marketing effectiveness and customer engagement.
• Provide support during weekends, public holidays, and after-hours events as required.
• Perform any other marketing, administrative, or project-related duties as reasonably requested by management.

The successful candidate should demonstrate:
• Proven experience in developing and implementing marketing initiatives.
• Strong knowledge of digital marketing and social media management.
• Excellent content creation, copywriting, and communication skills.
• Exceptional organisational, planning, and administrative abilities.
• Strong project management and coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
• Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving abilities.
• Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships with a variety of stakeholders.
• Ability to work independently, take initiative, and perform effectively under pressure.

POSITION PURPOSE
Responsible for overseeing and directing accounting functions on an operational level, including general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, fixed asset, and cost accounting. Responsible for analysing and reconciling detailed general ledger accounts as assigned. Keeps records and accounts accurate and current. Researches and resolves discrepancies and accounting errors. Completes related reports, summaries, and records. Creates monthly expense reports. Performs related clerical duties. Prepares periodic reports, reviews and reconciles data, and participates in the development of specialized financial data. Oversees and prepares entries and adjustments to Company records, files, and statements. Prepares financial and variance analyses as well as budget and rolling forecast.
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND BASIC DUTIES
1. Assumes responsibility for the accurate and timely completion of assigned accounting functions.
a. Reviews monthly Financial Reports and working paper files.
b. Reconciles general ledger accounts as assigned.
c. Completes required records and reports and maintains files as classified.
d. Prepares journal entries and balances work in more complicated accounting areas.
e. Completes various accounting functions in accordance with established policies and procedures, and applicable regulations including:
• Preparing trial balances from source documents.
• Preparing Balance Sheets and Income Statements.
• Preparing notes to the reports.
• Preparing monthly JV accounts where applicable.
• Filing copies of final monthly reports.
• Participate in annual audit.
• Balancing intercompany loan accounts.
• Maintaining Shareholders Loan Schedules.
• Reviewing and Releasing creditors payments.
• Prepare and review 1 – 3 year Budgets and Rolling Forecasts.
f. Report on financial income, including Management and Admin Fees on rental recoveries, Letting Commissions on new or renewed leases, and interest earnings.
g. Researches and resolves accounting errors and discrepancies.
2. Assumes responsibility for effectively researching, tracking, and resolving accounting problems and discrepancies.
3. Assumes responsibility for establishing and maintaining effective communication and coordination with area personnel and with management.
a. Maintains regular contact with Operations Managers and Property Managers in the departments to obtain information and/or to correct transactions.
b. Keeps management informed of area activities and of any significant problems.
c. Attends and participates in meetings as required.
4. Assumes responsibility for establishing and maintaining effective business relations and personal dealing with vendors, governmental agencies, and outside business and accounting professionals.
a. Responds to questions and problems politely and promptly.
b. Ensures that clients are properly informed.
c. Ensures that the Company’s professional reputation is projected and maintained.
5. Assumes responsibility for related duties as required or assigned.
a. Stays informed of developments in the accounting field and of changing governmental and legal requirements.
b. Completes special projects as assigned.
c. Ensures that Accounting Department work areas are clean, secure, and well maintained.
PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENTS
1. Accounting documents, records, and reports are accurate, current, and timely.
2. Accounting errors or discrepancies are promptly discovered and resolved (or referred).
3. Good communication and coordination exists with Company personnel. Assistance and support are provided as needed.
4. Management is appropriately informed of area activities.
5. Accounting functions are completed in accordance with established standards, policies, and procedures.
EDUCATION/CERTIFICATION:
Bachelor’s degree in accounting or an equivalent combination of experience and training.
REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE:
Technical knowledge of accounting concepts, practices, procedures, and financial reports.
Understanding of related regulations, statutes, and filing requirements.
Knowledge of related computer applications.
EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:
Three or more years of previous property accounting and property listed funds experience preferred.
JV ACCOUNTING EXPERIENCE WILL BE BENEFICIAL.
SKILLS/ABILITIES:
Well organized and detail oriented.
Able to meet deadlines and manage projects.
Good math skills.
Good attention to detail and accuracy.
Cooperative and willing to assist others.
Able to use PC, calculator, and other basic business machines.
Good EXCEL knowledge
Strong analytical skills.
Work under pressure
Understand Pivots

About iStore
iStore is the home of everything Apple and Africa’s largest Apple Premium Reseller. With more than 41 physical and online stores across Africa, we provide expert advice, Apple Authorised Repairs, Business and Education solutions, training, and technical support for everything Apple.
About the Role
We are looking for an experienced Credit Analyst to support the assessment and approval of customer finance applications across the iStore retail network.
This role is responsible for reviewing customer credit applications, assessing affordability and financial risk, and making sound credit decisions within agreed turnaround times. As our stores trade seven days a week, the successful candidate must be available to work retail hours, including weekends and public holidays.
The role requires someone who is analytical, decisive and customer-focused, while ensuring that all applications are assessed responsibly and in line with our credit policies and risk appetite.
Key Responsibilities
Credit Assessment and Decision-Making
• Review and analyse customer finance applications to determine creditworthiness and affordability.
• Make independent credit decisions within the required approval limits and service-level timeframes.
• Interpret credit bureau reports, customer financial information and supporting documentation.
• Identify potential credit, affordability, fraud and compliance risks.
• Approve, decline or refer applications in line with company credit policies and risk appetite.
• Clearly document the rationale for all credit decisions.
• Recommend appropriate risk-mitigation measures where required.
Customer and Portfolio Risk Management
• Monitor customer exposure, credit limits, risk ratings and account performance.
• Conduct regular credit reviews and ensure customer information remains accurate and up to date.
• Identify changes in customer risk profiles and escalate concerns where necessary.
• Support the responsible management of the consumer finance portfolio.
• Assist with the identification of trends, risks and potential areas of concern within the portfolio.
Retail and Business Support
• Provide efficient credit decision support to iStore teams across the retail network.
• Work closely with stores and internal stakeholders to resolve application queries and outstanding information.
• Balance responsible credit decision-making with the need to provide a positive customer experience.
• Communicate credit decisions clearly and professionally.
• Provide objective guidance on the risks, benefits and potential implications of applications.
• Support credit-related projects, reporting, data analysis and forecasting where required.
Qualifications and Experience
• Bachelor’s degree or relevant qualification in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Risk Management or a related field.
• Three to five years’ experience in credit analysis, consumer finance, retail finance, banking or a related environment.
• Experience assessing individual consumer credit applications.
• Strong understanding of the full credit lifecycle.
• Experience reading and interpreting credit bureau records.
• Sound knowledge of affordability assessments, financial analysis and credit risk principles.
• Experience working within credit policies, approval limits and service-level requirements.
• Proficiency in data analysis, reporting and Microsoft Excel.
• Experience in a high-volume retail or consumer finance environment would be advantageous.Working hours
This role supports a retail environment and requires flexibility to work:
• Weekends (Rotation, so not every weekend)
• Public holidays where required
• Retail trading hours
• Shifts or scheduled standby periods, where required
What we offer
• The opportunity to join a diverse team of passionate individuals.
• Exposure to one of the world’s leading technology brands.
• A fast-paced and challenging retail environment.
• The opportunity to expand your credit, risk and consumer finance experience.
• A role where your decisions directly support both the customer experience and the responsible growth of the business.
Competencies
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Sound judgement and the ability to make confident, objective decisions.
• High attention to detail and accuracy.
• Strong understanding of responsible lending and affordability principles.
• Ability to interpret complex credit and financial information.
• Good verbal and written communication skills.
• Strong time-management and organisational skills.
• Able to work effectively under pressure and manage high application volumes.
• Ethical, transparent and consistent in decision-making.
• Adaptable and comfortable working in a fast-paced retail environment.
• Strong relationship-building and stakeholder-management skills.
Background Checks
Should your application be successful, relevant background checks will be conducted. It will include criminal record, credit, identity, qualification and reference checks.

The Senior Analyst, Finance Systems Implementation acts as the functional-technical bridge between Finance, the IT organization, and external implementation partners across the company's strategic finance systems portfolio (ERP, Procurement platforms, Financial Consolidation tools, and related applications). This person is not the hands-on system builder or configurator — that work is delivered by implementation partners and IT specialists — but must understand technical implementation logic, system architecture, data flows, and integrations well enough to translate business requirements into technical specifications, challenge partner and IT proposals, anticipate downstream impacts, and ensure that finance processes are properly represented and protected throughout the project lifecycle.
Key Responsibilities
Project & Solution Interface
• Act as the primary point of contact between implementation partners, the internal IT team, and finance key users
during the design, build, testing, and deployment phases of ERP, Procurement, Consolidation, and related system
projects.
• Translate finance business requirements into functional and technical specifications that partners and IT can build
against, and translate technical constraints back into business terms for finance stakeholders.
• Review and validate solution designs, integration architecture, and data models proposed by implementation
partners, flagging risks, gaps, or misalignment with finance processes before they reach production.
• Facilitate decision-making across parties, escalating and resolving conflicts between technical feasibility and
business needs.
Technical & Data Oversight
• Maintain a working understanding of the systems' technical architecture, including modules in scope, master data
structures, and how the platform integrates with upstream and downstream systems.
• Map and validate end-to-end data flows across systems (e.g., Procurement to ERP, ERP to Consolidation, source
systems to reporting layers), ensuring data integrity, consistency, and traceability.
• Partner with IT and implementation teams on integration design (APIs, interfaces, batch/real-time flows), without
being responsible for coding or configuring integrations directly.
• Support test planning and execution (unit, integration, UAT) by defining business scenarios, validating results
against expected data outcomes, and coordinating key-user testing.
Governance & Change Management
• Ensure that documentation (process flows, data dictionaries, integration maps, functional specs) is complete,
current, and accessible to all stakeholders.
• Support change management and training efforts, helping key users understand new processes and system
behavior resulting from implementation.
• Monitor project milestones, risks, and dependencies related to the technical build, escalating issues that could
affect timeline, data quality, or financial control.
• Contribute to post-go-live assisted operation, hypercare and continuous improvement, identifying enhancement
opportunities and recurring data or integration issues.
Required Qualifications
• Education: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Information Technology / Information Systems,
Engineering, or a related field.
• Experience: 3+ years of experience directly involved in a finance systems implementation project (ERP,
Procurement, or Financial Consolidation), covering at least one full project phase — requirements, design, build,
testing, or deployment — whether on the business/finance side, the IT side, or as part of an implementation
partner team.
• Interface experience: Prior experience acting as a liaison between business, IT, and external
implementation/consulting partners during a systems project.
• Platform-specific experience: Direct, hands-on exposure to specific platforms such as SAP, Oracle, Sage or
Microsoft Dynamics (ERP); Coupa, Ariba, or Ivalua (Procurement); or OneStream, Hyperion, or SAP BPC/Group
Reporting (Consolidation) or similar platforms.
• Consulting background: Background as a consultant with a Big 4 or systems implementation partner (e.g.,
Deloitte, PwC, EY, Accenture) or other implementation partners active in South Africa.
• GCP: Knowledge of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) — familiarity with cloud data architecture, storage, and how
finance data is hosted and processed in a cloud environment.
• Fluence / Anaplan: Hands-on or functional exposure to Fluence and/or Anaplan, particularly for planning,
consolidation, or reporting use cases.
Technical & Functional Skills
• Finance process knowledge: Solid understanding of core finance processes (record-to-report, procure-to-pay,
financial consolidation, and reporting) and how they are represented in ERP/Procurement/Consolidation systems.
• Systems literacy: Ability to read and reason about system architecture diagrams, data models, and integration
designs (APIs, interfaces, middleware) without needing to build them personally.
• Data flow fluency: Comfortable working with data flows across systems; able to trace a data element from source
to report and identify where breaks or inconsistencies occur.
• Query/analysis tools: Working knowledge of SQL or data query tools is a strong plus, sufficient to
independently validate data rather than relying entirely on IT or partners.
• Project methodology: Familiarity with agile or hybrid project delivery methods, requirements gathering,
functional specification writing, and UAT/test management.
• Integration awareness: Ability to read integration/interface specifications and assess whether a proposed
technical solution meets the business requirement.
Soft Skills & Competencies
• Bridge communication: Comfortable operating between technical (IT/partners) and business (finance key users)
audiences, adjusting language and depth accordingly.
• Analytical rigor: Able to spot inconsistencies, risks, or gaps in complex system designs and processes before
they become production issues.
• Influence without authority: Confident challenging implementation partners and IT on technical proposals when
they do not serve the business need, while maintaining collaborative relationships.
• Organization: Structured, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple workstreams and stakeholders
simultaneously.
• Curiosity for technology: Genuine interest in how systems work — this role suits someone who enjoys
understanding the "plumbing" behind finance processes, not just the process itself.

Role Purpose
Own the commercial marketing performance of the Lending and Insurance portfolios, lead the marketing agenda within Growth & Engagement, and build the capability to grow it.
This is a senior, commercially-minded marketer who does more than run campaigns. They bring breadth across direct marketing, product, CX and UX, and contact centre, and use it to improve the whole customer experience, acquisition, conversion, engagement and value, across both verticals. They decide what needs to happen and why. The Campaign Specialist owns how and when.
Scope
Now
Own commercial marketing for Lending and Insurance. Direct the Campaign Specialist, partner CRM, and drive journey, conversion and CX improvements across both books.
Over Time
Take over management of Affiliates (from Pierre) to bring the capability in-house and reduce affiliate dependency. Build a product-marketing team as scale requires. Provide succession bench-strength for the Executive: Growth & Engagement role.
Core Responsibilities
• Commercial Marketing OwnershipOwn the commercial marketing performance of both portfolios, customer growth, conversion, engagement, retention, cross-sell and marketing effectiveness. Translate business objectives into marketing priorities and commercial recommendations for leadership.
• Customer Experience, Journeys and UXOwn the end-to-end customer journey across acquisition, onboarding, lifecycle, retention, reactivation and cross-sell. Use product, CX and UX experience to remove friction and improve conversion, not just messaging, but the experience itself. Work with CRM and the Campaign Specialist to implement.
• Customer InsightBuild a deep understanding of customers through research, behavioural analysis, complaints, call listening and contact-centre insight, competitor and market monitoring. Turn insight into marketing and experience improvements.
• Performance Analysis and RecommendationsMonitor performance across campaigns, channels, conversion, engagement and ROI. Present insight, root cause, recommendation and action. Never simply present data.
• Campaign Prioritisation and DirectionSet campaign priorities and brief the Campaign Specialist on objective, audience, messaging, offer and desired outcome. Review performance and optimise. This role directs campaigns; it does not produce them.
• Leadership and Capability BuildSet the marketing agenda for the portfolios, build and coach the team over time, and take on Affiliates when ready. Lead through ownership and influence, not administration.
• Stakeholder ManagementWork at a senior level with Product, Credit, Risk, Analytics, CRM, Contact Centre, Creative Studio, Compliance and Exco to ensure marketing supports the wider commercial agenda.
What Stays With Others
Campaign production, workflow, scheduling, asset management and compliance administration sit with the Marketing Campaign Specialist. Lifecycle orchestration and automation sit with CRM. This role briefs, prioritises and directs that work.
Primary KPIs
Success in the role is measured across both verticals through applications and funded loans, quotes and policies, conversion, silent rate, NTU, persistency and retention, cross-sell and 2+ product penetration, marketing ROI, and, in time, affiliate efficiency and customer-experience measures.
Candidate Profile
A senior marketer with genuine breadth, comfortable owning commercial outcomes and building capability.

• Breadth across direct marketing, product, CX/UX and contact centre
• Strong digital and CRM / customer-journey capability
• Commercial mindset, fluent in conversion, cost, quality and value
• Strong Excel and Power BI; comfortable with data (SQL desirable)
• Proven leadership and senior stakeholder management
• Potential to grow into an executive Growth & Engagement remit

Role Purpose
Own and grow the commercial performance of the insurance portfolio, funeral and accident products, by understanding the customer, building trust, and turning insight into marketing decisions that grow quotes, policy sales, persistency and customer value.
This is a product marketing role, not a campaign coordination role, and not a Head of Marketing role. The Marketing Manager spends their time on the questions that move the numbers, why conversions are changing, where customers drop off or fail to take up, which journeys need fixing, which campaigns to prioritise, what customers are telling us, and how to grow customer value, and turns the answers into recommendations for leadership.
They spend very little time chasing artwork, loading campaigns, building project plans, scheduling emails or coordinating approvals. That work belongs to the Marketing Campaign Specialist.
Where the Role Sits
This role sits within the Growth & Engagement division and reports to the Executive: Growth & Engagement.
The operating model deliberately separates commercial ownership from campaign execution. The Marketing Manager decides what needs to happen and why. The Marketing Campaign Specialist decides how it is delivered and when it launches. This role briefs, prioritises and guides execution. It does not run production.
Three Clear Owners
Executive: Growth & Engagement – Owns the Strategy
Growth strategy, commercial priorities and portfolio direction. Investment decisions, cross-product strategy and executive stakeholder management.
Marketing Manager (This Role) – Owns the Performance
Product marketing performance, customer insight and customer journeys. Campaign priorities, product positioning, commercial recommendations, marketing optimisation and stakeholder alignment.
Marketing Campaign Specialist – Owns the Delivery
Campaign execution and production, workflow and asset management, creative coordination, compliance approvals, scheduling and launches, and project management.
How the Role Spends Its Time
Approximately 30% of the role is focused on product marketing and commercial performance.
Approximately 25% of the role is focused on customer journey optimisation.
Approximately 15% of the role is focused on customer insight and research.
Approximately 15% of the role is focused on performance analysis and reporting.
Approximately 10% of the role is focused on stakeholder management.
Approximately 5% of the role is focused on executive presentations and planning.
Core Responsibilities
• Product Marketing OwnershipOwn the commercial marketing performance of the insurance portfolio. Be accountable for customer growth, conversion, engagement, retention, cross-sell and marketing effectiveness. Translate business objectives into clear marketing priorities.
• Customer Journey OptimisationOwn the ongoing optimisation of the end-to-end customer journey: acquisition, onboarding, abandoned journeys, lifecycle communications, retention, reactivation and cross-sell. Identify friction, quantify its impact, and recommend improvements. Work closely with CRM and the Campaign Specialist to implement enhancements.
• Customer InsightBuild a deeper understanding of the customer than anyone else in the business through surveys, customer interviews, complaints, behavioural analysis, call listening, competitor monitoring and market trends. Turn that insight into concrete marketing improvements.
• Performance AnalysisMonitor performance across campaigns, channels, customer behaviour, conversion, engagement and ROI. Present insight, root cause, recommendation and action.
Never simply present data. Every report ends with a decision or a recommendation.
• Campaign PrioritisationDevelop campaign briefs and priorities, and give the Campaign Specialist clear direction on objective, target audience, messaging, offer and desired outcome. Review campaign performance and continuously optimise. This role directs campaigns. It does not produce them.
• Stakeholder ManagementWork closely with Product, Credit, Risk, Analytics, CRM, Creative Studio, the Campaign Specialist, Compliance and Customer Service to ensure marketing activity supports broader commercial objectives.
Insurance Focus
Beyond the core, the Insurance Marketing Manager owns the commercial marketing of the funeral and accident portfolio specifically through:
• Quote generation and policy sales growth
• Building and protecting customer trust in the products
• NTU (not-taken-up) improvement, converting quotes and approvals into active policies
• Persistency, retention and premium growth
• Cross-sell of insurance from the lending base
• Clear, reassuring claims communications that reinforce trustPrimary KPIs
Success in the role is measured through the volume of insurance quotes generated and the number of new policies activated from quotes.
The role is measured on quote-to-policy conversion across the funnel and NTU (not-taken-up) rates on quoted or approved policies, where lower is better.
Additional measures include persistency, which reflects the retention of active policies over time, retention across the overall portfolio, and premium growth through growth in gross written premium (GWP).
The role is also measured on campaign ROI, reflecting the return on marketing spend by campaign and channel.
What This Role Is Not
To keep commercial ownership and execution cleanly separated, this role is explicitly not responsible for:
• Campaign production or campaign loading
• Creative traffic management
• Project management and workflow management
• Campaign scheduling
• Compliance administration
• Asset managementThese responsibilities belong to the Marketing Campaign Specialist. The Marketing Manager briefs, prioritises and guides that work. It does not perform it.
Candidate Profile
We are looking for a commercially minded product marketer, not a campaign coordinator and not a Head of Marketing. Someone who is happiest with a funnel, a data set and a customer problem in front of them.
• 5–8 years' marketing experience, ideally in financial services
• Strong digital marketing capability across acquisition and lifecycle
• Hands-on CRM and customer-journey experience
• Campaign planning and briefing experience
• A commercial mindset, fluent in conversion, cost and value, not just activity
• Strong Excel and Power BI capability; comfortable interpreting data independently
• Excellent written and verbal communication
• Strong stakeholder management across commercial and technical teams
• SQL is desirable but not mandatoryLeadership Expectations
This role may not carry direct reports from day one, but it is a leadership position. We expect ownership, accountability and initiative, someone who sets the commercial agenda for their portfolio, thinks like an operator, collaborates across functions, and influences outcomes through evidence rather than authority.
How Success Is Measured
Success is measured by commercial outcomes and the quality of thinking behind them, not by campaign administration or delivery activity.
Evidence of success includes:
• Improved conversion across the funnel
• Customer growth
• Campaign effectiveness and marketing ROI
• Measurable customer-journey improvements
• Cross-sell performance
• Customer engagement and retention
• The quality of commercial recommendations made to leadership
• Stakeholder satisfaction

Junior International Payroll Specialist (JB6191)
Location: Remote, South Africa
Salary: Market-related
Employment Type: Initial 12-month contract (Intended conversion to perm via of Employer of Record)
If you have built a solid payroll foundation and find yourself restless for something bigger, this is the role that turns that ambition into a career. A fast-growing international HR and payroll consultancy headquartered in the Netherlands is expanding its remote team and looking for a junior payroll specialist based in South Africa who is ready to move beyond local payroll and into the world of multi-country, multi-client international payroll operations. This is not a placeholder role while you wait for something else. It is a deliberate step into a specialist career path with real exposure, real responsibility and a team that has worked across every corner of the globe.
The successful candidate will join a consultancy that solves complex payroll puzzles for clients worldwide, stepping into different business environments, industries and operating models throughout their career. The team is built on expertise, curiosity and the willingness to keep learning as payroll legislation and global standards continue to evolve. Remote-first, internationally connected and genuinely invested in the growth of its people, this organisation rewards ambition and celebrates individuals who bring their whole selves to work.
This role is the launchpad. Starting with solid South African payroll experience as the foundation, the successful candidate will be developed into a specialist who can support increasingly complex multi-country payroll environments. Working alongside experienced global payroll professionals, the role offers hands-on exposure to international payroll operations, country-specific legislation, diverse payroll systems and direct client interaction from day one.
What's in it for you
Real international payroll exposure from early in your career, not years down the line
Mentorship from experienced global payroll consultants and a supportive team structure
Exposure to multiple payroll systems with training provided where needed
The opportunity to build knowledge across different countries, industries and client environments
A clear and intentional career path into international payroll specialisation
A high-energy team that encourages individuality, rewards curiosity and invests in continuous professional development
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in HR, Finance, Accounting, Commerce or a related field
2 to 3 years of practical payroll processing experience in South Africa
Exposure to payroll for at least one additional country outside South Africa is advantageous
Good understanding of payroll legislation, inputs, deductions, reconciliations and statutory deadlines
Experience using at least one recognised payroll system such as ADP, Workday, SAP, SD Worx, Sage, Deel, Remote, CloudPay or similar
Strong Microsoft Excel skills
Fluency in written and spoken English is essential
Proficiency in German, French, Italian or another European language is highly advantageous
A payroll qualification or certification is advantageous
A genuine long-term commitment to specialising in international payroll, not a stepping stone into generalist HR
Ability to work independently and communicate proactively in a fully remote environment
Key Responsibilities
Support the processing of payrolls for international clients across multiple countries
Assist with payroll validations and reconciliations
Coordinate with payroll providers and internal teams to meet deadlines
Respond to payroll queries from clients and employees in a professional and timely manner
Maintain payroll records, employee data and supporting documentation
Support year-end payroll activities and statutory compliance reporting
Document payroll processes and follow structured quality-assurance controls
Learn country-specific payroll legislation and requirements on an ongoing basis
Build capability across multiple payroll systems and platforms
Support continuous improvement initiatives within the payroll team
Build strong working relationships with colleagues, clients and payroll partners across different countries

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY
Are you a seasoned, hands-on production leader with a proven track record in heavy industrial manufacturing? We are looking for an experienced Production Foreman to take full operational control of shift operations for a leading continuous-process manufacturing plant.
This is not a desk job—we are seeking a highly visible, floor-focused leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, can manage a team of 30+ employees, and can make decisive, safety-first calls under pressure. Reporting directly to the Factory Manager, you will serve as the senior operational decision-maker on shift.

• Safety & Compliance (Section 8 Supervision): Enforce strict OHS standards, lead toolbox talks, maintain high housekeeping standards, and exercise authority to stop any unsafe work.
• Continuous Improvement: Track shift metrics (downtime, outputs, efficiency) and implement practical solutions to optimise energy use, labour productivity, and plant reliability.

Context
ForAfrika is an African-founded and led organisation with over 40 years of impact across the continent. We partner with communities through our integrated development continuum: saving lives and building resilience to reach self-sufficiency through our Humanitarian & Development work and unlocking commercial viability through our Social Enterprise activities. We are Africans, delivering African-led solutions for Africa, and we stand by our promise: we’re committed to the long run, until the job is done and communities are enabled to thrive.
The Design, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (DMEAL) unit represents a cornerstone of ForAfrika's commitment to evidence-based programming and continuous improvement across all humanitarian and development operations. Positioned at the leadership level within the Humanitarian and Development Division, DMEAL ensures that rigorous evidence generation, systematic learning, and adaptive management become embedded throughout ForAfrika's pursuit of its 2036 vision to empower 20 million Africans to be self-sufficient, with a further 6 million provided with a platform to thrive.
Within ForAfrika's organisational structure, DMEAL functions as both a technical service provider and a quality assurance mechanism, working with country offices to ensure that monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning systems meet international standards while remaining contextually appropriate and utilisation-focused. The unit directly supports ForAfrika's commitment to demonstrating impact to stakeholders, ensuring accountability to the communities served, and generating evidence that contributes to broader knowledge in humanitarian and development practice.
Core Purpose
The Knowledge Management Specialist is ForAfrika's central point for internal knowledge: capturing, curating, translating, and repackaging technical products from programme and DMEAL teams so that different technical audiences, across country offices and at global level, can find, understand, and apply them. This knowledge management function makes up approximately 60% of the role.
The remaining 40% is dedicated to reporting, treated as one of the organisation's most important knowledge products: reports underpin external accountability to donors and communities while feeding organisational learning about programme implementation. Here, the Specialist manages the reporting calendar, quality-assures reports against donor and organisational standards, and consolidates multi-country reports, applying the same standards of clarity and audience adaptation that guide the rest of the role.
Key Roles and Responsibilities
Knowledge Management (approximately 60% of time)
Knowledge Systems, Filing, and Digital Infrastructure
The Specialist builds and maintains the systems that make ForAfrika's institutional knowledge easy to find and reuse: knowledge repositories on SharePoint and Teams, filing structures and naming conventions that scale as content grows, and version control, access permissions, and security protocols that protect sensitive information while keeping the right content open across the organisation. The Specialist also develops templates and short guidance materials so country office teams can contribute without added administrative burden.
Responsible Use of AI for Knowledge Management
The Specialist builds an AI-enabled knowledge hub, using AI tools to tag, index, search, and synthesise content across the knowledge base. AI-assisted outputs must be checked for accuracy before sharing, clear rules govern what data can be processed through which tools, and colleagues are kept informed of where AI is used.
Learning Analysis and Multi-Format Communication
The Specialist analyses knowledge products across ForAfrika's portfolio, including evaluations, monitoring data, operational reviews, and programme documentation, to identify lessons on works, what doesn't, and under what conditions. Findings are translated into the format and language each audience needs, from learning briefs and infographics for field teams to technical annexes for specialists and short narratives for senior leadership, including good practice guides, lessons learned notes, and case studies.
Facilitation, Communities of Practice, and Innovation
The Specialist develops and facilitates communities of practice among ForAfrika staff, running discussion sessions, learning events, and cross-country exchanges. The Specialist is expected to bring new thinking to how the organisation captures and shares knowledge, testing new formats, tools, and facilitation approaches and adjusting them based on what colleagues actually use.
Matrix Relationships and Coordination
The Specialist supports country office DMEAL staff on local knowledge management practice, and coordinates with the Monitoring Systems Manager and the Evaluation and Research Manager so that monitoring and evaluation findings feed systematically into the knowledge base and learning priorities inform monitoring and evaluation planning.
Reporting (approximately 40% of time)
Reporting Calendar Management and Risk Coordination
The Specialist maintains the master reporting calendar for ForAfrika's portfolio. Country offices remain accountable for producing their reports; the Specialist tracks submission status, runs reminders ahead of deadlines, and flags emerging risks to country directors, the DMEAL Director, and senior management. This includes regular check-ins with country offices approaching major deadlines and facilitating planning conversations that set realistic timelines for multi-level review.
Report Quality Assurance and Tiered Compliance Coordination
The Specialist coordinates quality assurance using ForAfrika's three-tier country office system: selective sampling for Tier 1, systematic review of major donor and annual reports for Tier 2, and full review before submission for Tier 3. The Specialist maintains quality checklists covering narrative coherence, data accuracy, donor compliance, and inputs from the finance team.
Multi-Country Report Consolidation and Synthesis
For multi-country projects, the Specialist designs data compilation structures and narrative frameworks that keep reporting consistent across countries while leaving room for context, sets timelines and quality standards for country-level inputs. The Specialist then synthesises country inputs into a single report that presents a coherent picture of portfolio performance and surfaces cross-country learning without flattening it into one storyline.
Data Management and Analysis for Reporting
The Specialist works with the Monitoring Systems Manager to access, verify, and analyse programme data, formulating clear data requests that state what is needed, in what format, and by when, so monitoring systems can supply the data each report requires.
Capacity Building and Technical Support
The Specialist calibrates reporting support to each country office's tier: intensive guidance and draft review for Tier 3, targeted review of major reports for Tier 2, and lighter-touch consultation for Tier 1. This includes training on report writing, data presentation, and storytelling, reference materials such as templates and annotated examples, and individual coaching that builds authors' skills over time.

• Minimum 6 years of combined experience in knowledge management, organisational learning, and/or report writing and coordination, in humanitarian or development programmes
• Demonstrated experience designing and running knowledge management systems, including SharePoint, Teams, and filing/document management systems
• Experience using AI tools for content organisation, tagging, search, or synthesis, with an understanding of data se

The Inbound Controller: Import & Export is responsible for managing and controlling the end-to-end import and export flow of goods to warehouses, distribution centers, or directly to clients. The role ensures that all shipments are executed accurately, compliantly, cost-effectively, and timeously, in accordance with SARS customs regulations, trade requirements, and company standards
Key Responsibilities
1. Pre-Shipment & Trade Coordination (Import & Export)
Liaise with international suppliers and export partners to confirm goods readiness, packaging, labelling standards, and shipping deadlines.
Verify and apply correct Incoterms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, etc.).
Book freight with approved freight forwarders across sea, air, road, and rail transport modes.
Request, validate, and manage all import and export shipping documentation prior to shipment departure.
2. Import & Export Documentation & Customs Clearance
Manage all import and export customs documentation via the internal customs management system.
Ensure customs clearance is completed prior to vessel arrival (imports) or cargo departure (exports).
Prepare, review, submit, and archive SAD500 declarations for imports and exports.
Ensure accurate preparation and compliance of export documentation, including:
Commercial invoices
Packing lists
Bills of Lading / Air Waybills / Sea Waybills
Certificates of Origin (SADC, EUR1, where applicable)
Export permits and licences (where applicable)
HS tariff classifications and customs valuation
Ensure compliance with the SARS Customs & Excise Act and applicable exchange control regulations.
Support and participate in SARS audits, inspections, and regulatory reviews.
Apply working knowledge of customs stops, border police inspections, NRCS stops, and export control requirements.
Liaise with clearing agents on inspections, queries, SAD500 amendments, and customs or invoicing discrepancies.
Update internal systems with customs clearance and shipment status.
3. Shipment Tracking & Control
Track shipments from origin to final destination.
Monitor ETD/ETA, transhipments, route changes, and delays.
Proactively communicate shipment status, risks, and delays to internal stakeholders.
Conduct daily follow-ups with clearing agents, transporters, and relevant parties.
4. Warehouse, Inventory & Delivery Coordination
Maintain accurate container and inventory control.
Coordinate the timely receiving and unloading of inbound containers.
Schedule deliveries and collections in line with operational requirements.
Process direct deliveries via the sales system.
Book deliveries upon receipt of IODs and PODs.
Verify received goods against documentation and report shortages or damages.
5. Client & Internal Support
Support internal teams and clients with import and export-related queries.
Coordinate delivery and collection dates.
Assist with shipping, customs, and sales-related queries.
Maintain professional and effective communication with all stakeholders.
Support issue resolution and escalation where required.
6. Cost Control & Performance Monitoring
Monitor and control freight costs, demurrage, detention, and storage charges.
Support cost optimisation initiatives.
Track and support KPIs, including:
On-time delivery performance
Customs clearance lead times
Import and export cost variances
Documentation and SAD500 accuracy
Tools & Systems
Customs management systems
ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, or similar)
Warehouse Management Systems (WMS)
Transport Management Systems (TMS)
Microsoft Word, Excel (advanced), PowerPoint, and Outlook

job_title: Sea Freight Operator / Ocean Freight Operator
about_role:
The Sea Freight Operator is responsible for the day-to-day operational handling of import and export ocean freight shipments. The role focuses on bookings, documentation, and coordination with shipping lines, agents, transporters, and internal teams to ensure efficient and compliant cargo movement for both FCL and LCL shipments.
Key Responsibilities
1. Ocean Freight Operations
Manage end-to-end sea freight operations for FCL and LCL shipments
Process import and export ocean freight files
Coordinate vessel bookings with shipping lines and NVOCCs
Monitor vessel schedules, cut-offs, rollovers, and transhipments
Track shipments to ensure timely delivery
2. Documentation Handling
Prepare, verify, and submit all required sea freight documentation, including:
Master Bill of Lading (MBL)
House Bill of Lading (HBL)
Shipping Instructions
Commercial Invoices
Packing Lists
Delivery Orders
Ensure accuracy and compliance with customs and trade regulations
Manage document amendments and corrections with relevant parties
3. Coordination & Communication
Liaise with overseas agents, shipping lines, terminals, and transporters
Coordinate with customs brokers for cargo clearance
Communicate shipment updates, ETAs, and delays to customers and internal teams
Resolve operational issues such as delays, demurrage, and detention
4. Import & Export Handling
Manage export cargo cut-offs and port gate-in timelines
Coordinate import deliveries, container tracking, and empty returns
Monitor free time and minimize demurrage and detention costs
Ensure timely cargo release and delivery order processing
5. Cost Control & Billing Support
Verify freight costs, local charges, and supplier invoices
Ensure job files are complete and ready for billing
Support finance with accurate operational data
Identify and report cost discrepancies impacting profitability
6. Systems & Compliance
Capture and update shipment data in TMS/ERP systems (e.g., CargoWise)
Utilize Trade Tech systems (RCG) where applicable
Maintain accurate shipment records and documentation
Adhere to company SOPs and compliance requirements
Support audits and reporting processes

Our client in the mining and metals sector is recruiting a Senior Commissioning Manager to lead commissioning activities on large-scale minerals processing projects. This role is ideal for a highly analytical professional who enjoys solving complex business problems, working with large datasets, and collaborating with both business and technical stakeholders to deliver impactful solutions. You will be responsible for analysing and designing solutions that support business intelligence, reporting, financial modelling, and operational excellence initiatives.
Key Responsibilities
• Analyse and design solutions for digital transformation initiatives.
• Engage with stakeholders to understand current business processes, systems, reporting structures, and future-state requirements.

• Define, document, and present solution recommendations to stakeholders.

• Design and implement reporting solutions, dashboards, and analytics frameworks.
• Develop financial and operational models that support strategic decision-making.
• Perform detailed process and data analysis to understand how information flows across systems and reporting environments.
• Identify opportunities for automation, optimisation, and continuous improvement.
• Assist in identifying risks and challenges related to solution implementation.
• Translate business and system requirements into functional specifications for development teams.
• Build strong stakeholder relationships and ensure successful delivery against business objectives.
• Provide expert guidance on improving data quality, reporting effectiveness, and overall business intelligence capabilities.
Requirements
Experience & Qualifications
• Minimum 5-8 years' experience in Data Analysis, Business Analysis, or a related field.
• Strong experience working with large data sets and data-driven solutions.
• Experience working with financial systems and financial system integrations.
• Solid understanding of data warehousing concepts and methodologies.

• Experience supporting reporting, business intelligence, and analytics initiatives.
• Technical & Professional Skills
• Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.
• Strong systems thinking and solution design skills.
• Expertise in data profiling, data quality assessment, and data scoping.
• Ability to identify inefficiencies and recommend process improvements.
• Experience translating complex requirements into clear technical specifications.
• Ability to communicate technical concepts effectively to both business and technical audiences.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Naturally curious with a passion for technology and innovation.
Personal Attributes
• Proactive and solution-oriented mindset.
• Detail-oriented and highly organised.
• Comfortable working in fast-paced, evolving environments.
• Able to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
• Thrives under pressure and works effectively to tight deadlines.

This is an opportunity to work with a leading organisation on strategic digital transformation initiatives, where your expertise in data analysis, business intelligence, and solution design will have a direct impact on business outcomes. You will collaborate with experienced professionals, work on meaningful projects, and contribute to shaping innovative data-driven solutions.

Introduction to the VKB Group
The VKB Group is an agricultural company, providing support to farmers and producing straight-from-the farm-foods for consumers. Apart from the various consumer brands, the VKB Group is also represented by its regional brands: VKB, GWK and NTK. Our roots are firmly planted in agriculture with farming at our core, continuously growing and evolving throughout the years.
Starting with providing everything needed on the farm to produce food, we now also operate in all areas of the food supply chain: processing, logistics, and national and global market channels.
This “house of brands” we’ve established with the support of our farmer shareholders is the foundation for building the agribusiness of the future.
Who We Are
At VKB Group, we believe in growth that is rooted in humility, driven by hunger, guided by smart thinking, made bold by innovation, and strengthened by teamwork. With deep roots in agriculture, we are committed to supporting farmers, producing straight-from-the-farm foods, and building an agribusiness for the future.
Our Mechanisation division plays a key role in keeping agriculture moving forward by supplying farmers with the right equipment, parts, and solutions when they need them most.
The Opportunity
We are looking for a Parts Marketer to join our team in Prieska, Northern-Cape. This is more than just a sales role—it’s about building lasting partnerships with farmers, understanding their needs, and ensuring they have the right parts to succeed.
If you are someone who is:
• Humble enough to learn from others and serve our customers first,
• Hungry to achieve goals and grow your career,
• Smart in solving problems and finding opportunities,
• Bold in taking initiative and driving results,
• A true Team Player who thrives in collaboration,then you might be exactly who we’re looking for.
What You’ll Do
• Drive sales of agricultural parts, accessories, and solutions while meeting agreed targets (commission applicable).
• Manage stock effectively, ensuring availability, ordering based on movement, and sourcing scarce parts quickly.
• Build strong, trust-based relationships with farmers and clients.
• Stay up to date with agricultural technologies and equipment to serve customers better.
• Take responsibility for the point-of-sale process including cash and card transactions.
• Maintain excellent housekeeping of stock and displays.
• Commit to continuous training and growth, both personally and professionally.What You’ll Need
• Grade 12 / NQF 4 with Mathematics.
• Proven sales and marketing experience in parts (essential).
• Knowledge of and passion for agriculture.
• Ability to work well under pressure.
• A strong customer service orientation.
• Computer literacy (Microsoft Office).
• Excellent communication, negotiation, and conflict management skills.Why VKB?
• Join a team that values growth, learning, and collaboration.
• Be part of a proudly South African agricultural group with strong farmer roots.
• Work in an environment where bold ideas are encouraged, and teamwork drives success.
• Competitive remuneration including performance-based commission. Other Information
